source: OpenStreetMap natural=coastline via Overpass API (data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0)
note: Continental Portugal coastal band ONLY (v2) — Madeira and the Azores are not covered. Eastern limit is lon -7.30 (a few km east of the Guadiana / Spanish border at Vila Real de Santo Antonio), so the whole Algarve — Albufeira, Portimao, Lagos, Faro, Olhao, Tavira, VRSA — is inside the bbox and routable; task 16's bbox stopped at -8.4 and left the eastern Algarve with charts but no routing. Land/water only: coastline rasterised conservatively at ~100 m (a cell is land if the shoreline touches it at all), flood-filled from the open sea so a cell is navigable only if it is genuinely connected to the sea, then every cell within 200 m of mapped land is reclassified as land — the shoreline survey, the raster and the sand itself are all less precise than that. Deliberately over-marks land: channels, river mouths and harbour entrances narrower than ~400 m are closed. Carries NO depth, tide, current, or charted-hazard information — route suggestions built from it avoid land, nothing else. Not for navigation.
